title: Raw cohomology admits an abelian complex presentation
statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring, k:W→S a scheme morphism, G a Λ-module sheaf on W_et, q∈ℤ, I a small cofiltered category, and D:I→Over W an inverse system with affine transition morphisms [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Assume every composite D(i)→S is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let c be a cone whose underlying scheme cone is limiting, and assume c.pt→S is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For an affine etale U→S, write P_i(U)=Hom((D(i)→S)^*Λ[U][0],D(i)^*G[q]) and P_c(U)=Hom((c.pt→S)^*Λ[U][0],c.pt^*G[q]) in D⁺ of module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For the raw diagram $H$ and cocone $B$ of [def-sbc-higher-image-raw-diagram], an abelian complex presentation [def-sbc-etale-complex-cohomology-presentation] exists. This is an identification of diagrams and their canonical maps, not a cohomology continuity assertion.

proof.text: Use the explicit diagram X_i=D(i) times_S U and its base-changed cone. Base change preserves the limiting cone and affine transitions. Each stage is qcqs because its map to affine U is qcqs. Put the underlying abelian pullbacks of G in single complexes of degree zero; the uniform lower bound is zero. Inverse-image composition supplies the coherent transition maps.

On the limit choose the constant diagram with the single complex of the underlying pullback of G. Inverse-image composition identifies it with the stage pullbacks. Its identity cocone is colimiting by connectedness of I opposite.

Take p=q and the canonical derived-adjunction map P. Free-module-sheaf adjunction and restriction to the etale fibre product identify the raw Hom groups with module cohomology. An injective module resolution computes the underlying abelian cohomology by all-object abelian section acyclicity. Naturality of derived adjunction, single-functor comparison, and shift comparison identifies the canonical cohomology transition and cocone equations with the five factors of each fixed raw pullback. These additive isomorphisms and canonical equations, together with the first two steps, supply all witnesses of the presentation. Negative degrees are zero on both sides.
